pull.title: wallet: reject unknown options in sendall
pull.body:
`sendall` silently ignores unknown keys in its `options` object, including misspelled ones: `input` instead of `inputs` spends all available UTXOs rather than the given ones, and a misspelled `add_to_wallet` or `psbt` can broadcast a transaction the caller asked not to broadcast.

Reject unknown options, like `send`, `fundrawtransaction`, `walletcreatefundedpsbt` and `bumpfee` already do.

committer Thomas <thomas.giudici@proton.me> 1792153573 +0200

wallet: reject unknown options in sendall

Unknown keys in the options object were silently ignored, so a typo
such as "input" for "inputs" spent all available UTXOs rather than the
given ones. The options are checked before the fee arguments are merged
into them, so that a misspelled estimate_mode is reported as an
unexpected key. The check also rejects the outdated camelCase names, so
sendall no longer needs PreventOutdatedOptions.

Minor nit:
`unknown` (or `unsupported`) options seem enough, probably?
This call can be removed now? Also, what about `send`?
Please squash your commits according to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#squashing-commits
Removed and squashed - `send` still needs it since `FundTransaction` accepts the camelCase names for `fundrawtransaction`

> Removed and squashed - `send` still needs it since `FundTransaction` accepts the camelCase names for `fundrawtransaction`

huh, `PreventOutdatedOptions` is called in `send` and it literally rejects all camelCase?

Using LLMs is fine, but you'll have to read and understand all code yourself as well.

I meant the call can't be dropped from `send` like it was from `sendall`. `send`'s options go through the `RPCTypeCheckObj` in `FundTransaction`, which allows the camelCase names `PreventOutdatedOptions` checks for, since they are `fundrawtransaction` options. So in `send` that call is what rejects them. The new list in `sendall` doesn't have them so the call was redundant there.

ok, hmm. I was thinking to add the type and field checks right in the RPC that needs them, not through some deeper calls, which accept camelCase, and then some more extra calls which reject it again.

But maybe this would be too much of a refactor. So seems fine to leave as-is for now.

I had a branch to remove all of this code anyway, but it was in tmpfs and I poured tea over my machine and lost it. Maybe I'll try to re-create it after https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36489 is merged.
